Defiant Dinusha helps Sri Lanka draw second Test, India win series 1-0
item.description:
Sonal Dinusha hit an unbeaten 133 as Sri Lanka staged a stunning comeback to draw the second Test against India in Colombo on Thursday.
Sri Lanka declared their second innings on 429-9 in the final session on day five after being made to follow on and the teams then shook hands before the 15 mandatory overs began.
India won the opening Test and claimed the two-match series 1-0.
Sri Lanka, who resumed on 229-6, extended their lead to 216 runs, the left-handed Dinusha standing out with twin centuries in the match after his 103 in the first innings.
India had looked favourites to wrap up the Test until day four, but overnight batters Dinusha and Keshara Nuwantha (46) put on 112 runs for the seventh wicket to turn the match on its head.
Left-arm spinner Manav Suthar broke the stand in the first over after lunch to have Nuwantha caught at second slip following a wicketless first session.
Veteran spinner Ravindra Jadeja then had Prabath Jayasuriya out for two but Dinusha kept up the fight with the lower-order.
India, who posted 503-9 declared in their first innings, enforced the follow-on after they bowled out Sri Lanka out for 290.
The hosts were in trouble at 218-6 in their second innings before Dinusha and Nuwantha ground their way towards an unlikely draw.

item.title: Police probe 'assault allegations' after Carse's nightclub incident
item.description:
Derbyshire Police are looking into "allegations of assault" following the incident that saw England fast bowler Brydon Carse handcuffed outside a nightclub over the weekend.
Carse was dropped from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan, which begins at Lord's on Thursday, after the Cricket Regulator initiated a probe into an episode that saw the Durham paceman arrested outside a late bar in Derby –- then de-arrested after agreeing to depart.
In an updated statement issued late Wednesday, Derbyshire Police said: "We are investigating allegations of assault in Derby city centre. No arrests have yet been made and the investigation is ongoing."
Further details are unknown, with no clarity over what part –- if any –- Carse had in the alleged assault, with the England and Wales Cricket Board yet to comment publicly on the latest developments.
An initial statement from the force, released after a video clip of Carse apparently being detained by officers in the street, had said: "A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre on Saturday night. However the man was de-arrested shortly afterwards having agreed to leave the area."
Former England captain Ben Stokes and centrally contracted seamer Matthew Potts both appeared in the footage, captured in the aftermath of their Durham side's County Championship victory over Derbyshire, though there is no suggestion either was involved in anything untoward.
Stokes's successor as Test skipper, Joe Root, spoke angrily Tuesday about the latest in a growing list of alcohol-related incidents that have engulfed the England set-up.
Root, who abolished the midnight curfew that contributed to Stokes's exit following another controversial night out earlier this season, said: "If I'm being brutally honest I'm really hacked off.
"I've spoken to Brydon and when I first found out my first concern was him as a person. I don't think I'm speaking out of turn in saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions."
Root added: "But it's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact we continuously keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we are doing on the field."

item.title: Bumrah's reign over as Starc claims No.1 Test ranking
item.description:
Jasprit Bumrah's tenure as the No.1 ranked Test bowler is over as Australia pacer Mitchell Starc claimed the premier position for the first time in his illustrious career on the back of his dominant performance against Bangladesh.
Bumrah first rose to the top back in February of 2024 and the right-armer has maintained his spot as the No.1 ranked Test bowler for much of the last two years.
But his absence from India's ongoing ICC World Test Championship series against Sri Lanka, coupled with Starc's recent Player of the Series heroics against Bangladesh has seen a significant change at the top of the ICC Men's Test Bowler Rankings.
Starc collected 10 wickets for the match in the second Test against Bangladesh in Mackay and that proved enough to catapult the 36-year-old up two places and past Bumrah and New Zealand pacer Matt Henry and into the prized position for the very first time in his career.
The Australian has been inside the top 10 for much of his 15-year Test career and recently entered the top three on the back of some strong efforts against England in the Ashes series towards the end of last year, but this is the first time he has risen all the way to the top.
Bumrah drops to second and Henry to third due to Starc's rise, while his Australian teammate Pat Cummins jumps one place to fourth on the same list for Test bowlers following his six wickets for the match during the clash against Bangladesh and spinner Nathan Lyon rises two spots to 10th.
There are also gains on the rankings for Test bowlers for England duo Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue following their match-winning efforts against Pakistan in the first Test in Headingley.
The pair combined for 16 wickets across the one-sided contest in Leeds, with Robinson jumping 15 spots to 11th place as Tongue improves 16 rungs to 17th overall.
The top of the Test batter rankings remains the same, with England duo Harry Brook (first) and Joe Root (second) holding a slender advantage over Australia pair Steve Smith (third) and Travis Head (fourth).
The big mover inside the top 10 is India's Rishabh Pant, with the left-hander gaining six spots to rise to equal seventh following his quickfire half-century in the second innings of his side's victory over Sri Lanka in the first Test in Galle.
Outside the top 10 there are gains on the list for Test batters for Australia all-rounder Cameron Green (up nine spots to 21st), Sri Lanka captain Dhananjaya de Silva (up two places to equal 22nd), Pakistan's Abdullah Shafique (up seven rungs to equal 27th) and India right-hander KL Rahul (up five slots to 30th).
It's also status quo on the updated rankings for Test all-rounders as India veteran Ravindra Jadeja maintains his place in the No.1 spot, as Cummins (up one spot to seventh), Green (up one place to equal 17th) and Robinson (up five rungs to 23rd) all make small gains.

item.title: Czech duo Muchova and Mensik win US Open mixed doubles title
item.description:
The Czech team of Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik won the US Open mixed doubles Wednesday, saving two match points in a nervy semi-final and then pulling through in a tight final.
The pair survived a second-set pummeling in the championship decider in New York to edge Belinda Bencic of Switzerland and Flavio Cobolli of Italy, 6-3, 1-6, 10-6.
Mensik, a singles semi-finalist at this year's French Open, sealed the triumph with a searing ace to the backhand corner.
Another Mensik ace saved one of two match points earlier in the evening when the Czech pair edged the Russians Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev, 5-4, 3-5, 11-9.
The back-to-back wins secured the first Grand Slam title for both Mensik and Muchova, who lost a heartbreaking Wimbledon singles final in July in three sets to fellow Czech, Linda Noskova.
"At the end the matching outfits made the difference for us," Muchova quipped during the trophy presentation, referencing the white and maroon kit worn by the team.
The mixed doubles event is in its second year with a convention-busting format which features shortened sets and multiple matches played the same day.
The competition is scheduled before the main US Open to attract singles stars who usually avoid Grand Slam doubles events to conserve energy for the concluding matches of the biggest events.
The tournament's star teams -- the cross-generational partnership of Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka -- did not make it through the event's preliminary rounds.
That left open a Grand Slam opportunity for some of the game's most accomplished non-household names to nab a precious major title, resulting two semifinals and a final that all went the distance.
Earlier, Cobolli and Bencic beat the married team of Elina Svitolina of Ukraine and Gael Monfils of France in a hard-fought marathon, 4-5, 4-1, 10-5.
The result ended the prospects for a fairytale finale to the career of the acrobatic Monfils, who has said 2026 will be his last season.

item.title: Savio scores on debut as Spurs set-up League Cup tie with Liverpool
item.description:
Savio scored on his Tottenham debut and was then challenged by manager Roberto De Zerbi to hit double figures for the season as Spurs advanced to a third-round League Cup tie with Liverpool following a comfortable 5-1 win over Charlton on Wednesday.
Spurs, four-times winners of the League Cup, started their Premier League season with a humiliating 3-0 loss away to Brentford last weekend.
But it was a different story at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, with two goals in four minutes late in the first half from Mikey Moore and Dominic Solanke leaving the hosts in command.
Substitute Kevin Danso scored with his first touch, meeting a free-kick with a flicked header in the 67th minute.
Brazilian winger Savio, who joined Spurs for a reported initial fee of £75 million ($102 million) from Manchester City, came off the bench and started to repay some of that outlay when he ran inside and beat two defenders before letting fly with an 82nd-minute shot inside the near post.
Barely three minutes later the player formerly known as Savinho paved the way for his side's fifth goal when his shot deflected in off Spurs captain Ben Davies's thigh.
Second-tier Charlton did manage a consolation goal against their London rivals when defender Lloyd Jones headed in from a corner.
"Yes, it is a perfect day for him," De Zerbi said of Savio.
"I spoke with him and we put the goal on 10 or 12 goals (target) because we need 10 or 12 goals from the wingers.
"Last season we suffered too much because also the number of goals were not enough to compete for nothing more than that (17th) position."
The nine Premier League teams that are playing in Europe -- Arsenal, Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton, Crystal Palace, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Sunderland -- all enter the League Cup in the third round.
The draw for that took place after Wednesday's games, with Spurs away to Liverpool in one of a possible six all-Premier League ties that will see Andrew Robertson make a quick return to Anfield following his summer move to Tottenham.
Manchester United face Brighton, while Chelsea will play Leeds if Xabi Alonso's side get past Luton on Thursday.
Premier League champions Arsenal travel to Ipswich, while League Cup holders Manchester City are at home to Norwich.
Elsewhere, Harvey Barnes scored twice against his old club on Wednesday as Newcastle edged Championship side West Brom 3-2.
Everton were too strong for Preston, winning 4-0 away to the club where Toffees boss David Moyes made his name as a manager, with Thierno Barry scoring a hat-trick.
Everton were drawn at home to Wolves, who finished bottom of the Premier League last season.
In Wednesday's other League Cup tie, third-tier leaders Bradford beat Burnley, also relegated from the Premier League last season, 4-2 on penalties following a goalless draw, with no extra time at this stage of the competition.
The third-round ties will be played on the weeks commencing September 7 and September 14.

item.title: Mbappe hits treble as Real Madrid thrash Real Sociedad
item.description:
Kylian Mbappe scored a brilliant hat-trick to help Real Madrid thrash Real Sociedad 4-1 in La Liga in Jose Mourinho's first home match back at the Santiago Bernabeu as the club's coach.
Mourinho's Madrid made it two wins from two with Vinicius Junior also on the scoresheet, while Jude Bellingham provided two assists as the star trio picked apart their Basque visitors.
Veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho selected the same side that snatched a late 2-1 win at Espanyol in his first match at the helm last Saturday.
Mourinho said it would be tricky but not impossible to get the team's three biggest names in the same team all at their best, and this match suggested he is on the right track.
"This guy is incredible," said Mourinho of Mbappe, while also praising Madrid's overall display.
"I see him really hungry to make history with Real Madrid, and I see a team where, despite Kylian being Kylian, it's hard for me not to talk about the team."
Vinicius fired over and Alex Remiro saved low at his near post from Mbappe during an open start to the game. At the other end, Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made a smart stop from Mikel Oyarzabal.
Remiro was called into action again to deny Vinicius after Mbappe slipped in the Brazil international, while La Real's Sergio Gomez sent a volley screaming just wide of Courtois's far post.
Five minutes before half-time, Madrid found the breakthrough, with Federico Valverde feeding Mbappe.
The French forward, top scorer in La Liga in each of the last two seasons, took a clever touch to escape his marker and buried the ball in the top corner to claim the first goal of his campaign.
"It's spectacular, incredible (to have Mbappe), we have to enjoy Mbappe and make the most of him as possible," captain Valverde told Real Madrid TV.
"We have to give him a thousand balls so he is comfortable, he can score goals, and he's happy."
However, Los Blancos could not survive to the break without conceding the equaliser against last season's Copa del Rey winners.
Job Ochieng dallied on the ball and his shot was blocked, but it fell nicely to Luka Sucic, who rammed home with the help of a deflection off Alvaro Carreras.
Valverde said that Madrid tweaked their approach to pressing in the second half and it paid dividends.
"We were finding it hard to get the ball back in their half... We adjusted that and in the second half we were a lot more comfortable," explained the Uruguayan midfielder.
Arda Guler played in Mbappe, whom Remiro denied early in the second half, but the Spanish goalkeeper could do nothing about the former Paris Saint-Germain star's next effort.
A neat move involving Valverde and then Bellingham led to the latter playing in Mbappe, who calmly stroked home. Madrid's third came from Vinicius, who had been quiet to this point, and he had the tenacity of Bellingham to thank.
The England midfielder's shot was blocked but he refused to give up, winning the ball back in Real Sociedad's area and putting it on a plate for Vinicius to tap home.
The Brazilian, brought to life by his goal, set up Mbappe with a perfectly weighted pass for the striker's third, a dink over Remiro which was the pick of the goals.
Vinicius, substituted with seven minutes to go for record Madrid signing Yan Diomande, embraced Mourinho after being brought off with the job done.
Madrid's previous campaign began to turn for the worse when Vinicius showed his anger after being replaced by Xabi Alonso during Madrid's Clasico win over Barcelona in October, but the forward, who recently extended his club deal until 2032, was all smiles.
"I liked everything, and you might tell me the second half was good and the first half wasn't, but I liked the team even when it wasn't good," said a satisfied Mourinho.
"I'm really happy that the players ended up content, winning at home, smiling, and tomorrow -- training -- because on Sunday comes Malaga."
On Thursday, Spanish champions Barcelona host Athletic Bilbao with new signing Rodri poised to make his debut for Hansi Flick's side from the bench.

item.title: Chinese faculty shares tax sharing, land finance models for Bangladesh
item.description:
With Bangladesh seeking structural solutions to broaden its narrow domestic revenue base, the Policy Research Institute of Bangladesh (PRI) gathered leading fiscal policymakers, economic analysts, and former revenue officials to analyze China's tax trajectory.
Delivering a special lecture titled “Taxation System and Reform in China: Lessons for Revenue Mobilization in Bangladesh,” Prof Ping Zhang, vice dean of the School of International Relations and Public Affairs at Fudan University, detailed how China leveraged indirect taxation and local resource mobilization to finance modern infrastructure development.

Key lessons from China's tax evolution
The lecture outlined two pivotal milestones in China's economic transformation.
The first was the 1984–1985 profit-to-tax reform for State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs), which transformed state profit remittances into a standardized corporate tax framework.
The second was the landmark 1993–1994 Tax-Sharing System reform. By centralizing half of all national tax collections, the central government secured national fiscal control.
However, this created a fiscal deficit at local government levels, directly giving rise to China's "land finance" model—a mechanism where municipal authorities monetized land-use rights to independently finance urban development.
"China’s fiscal trajectory shows a heavy reliance on indirect taxation, with VAT acting as the dominant revenue pillar," explained Prof Ping Zhang of Fudan University.
"The shift toward centralized tax sharing forced municipal authorities to innovate through land finance. For Bangladesh to scale its revenue base, it must modernize local property valuation, enforce strict property tax collections, and establish clear fiscal boundaries between central and regional administration tiers."

item.title: DCCI urges traders to engage in digital revenue management
item.description:
Taskeen Ahmed, president of the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry (DCCI), called upon traders to increase their involvement in automated revenue management and digital processes to overcome existing hurdles in tax payment, alongside ensuring compliance with laws and regulations in overall business operations.
He made this call on Thursday (August 27) while inaugurating a workshop titled "Changes and Modifications in VAT, Tax, Customs Laws, and Personal E-Return Management in the FY2026-27 Budget" held at the DCCI Auditorium.
Nirjhar Ahmed, Additional Commissioner of the Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate, Dhaka (West) under the National Board of Revenue (NBR), attended the workshop as a special guest.
In his opening remarks, Taskeen Ahmed stated that the government has introduced several changes to VAT, income tax, customs, and e-return systems in the current fiscal year's budget. It is essential for traders to have a clear understanding of these revised policies, as this will help ensure proper compliance with laws and regulations in business operations.
He further noted that to avoid various obstacles in paying taxes and to increase tax contribution to GDP, the government is emphasizing automated and digital revenue management. Entrepreneurs must acquire the necessary knowledge regarding the opportunities and processes of this system.
In his speech as the special guest, Nirjhar Ahmed said that by paying revenue, the country's entrepreneurs make a significant financial contribution to various development initiatives of the government. Therefore, to ensure compliance across all aspects of business, entrepreneurs must stay aware of the updated rules in revenue management.
He informed that in the current fiscal year's budget, VAT registration or a Business Identification Number (BIN) has been made mandatory for several services, including obtaining and renewing trade licenses, opening bank accounts, and acquiring or renewing membership in trade organizations.
He urged entrepreneurs who do not yet have a VAT registration to complete it promptly.
Nirjhar Ahmed added that under Section 64 of the VAT Act, the opportunity to submit VAT returns has been extended from one tax period to three tax periods, which will make return management easier for business owners.
Furthermore, he stated that the previous requirement to deposit 10 percent of the demanded tax when appealing to the Appellate Tribunal has been amended. Under the new provision, the deposit rate has been set at 1 percent for the Appellate Tribunal and 2 percent for appeals to the High Court. He expressed hope that this will significantly reduce the financial burden on traders.
The workshop featured two separate sessions focusing on income tax and Value Added Tax (VAT). Snehasish Barua, adviser to DCCI's Standing Committee on Customs & VAT, and Md Shafiqul Alam, Joint Convener of the committee, presented the keynote papers.

item.title: Prime Bank, Square Toiletries to enhance receivables management efficiency
item.description:
Prime Bank PLC has entered into an agreement with Square Toiletries Limited to provide a customized receivables management solution aimed at enhancing collection efficiency, reconciliation, and transparency across Square Toiletries’ nationwide distribution network.
Under the agreement, distributors of Square Toiletries across Bangladesh will make payments through unique virtual accounts.
The solution will enable automated identification and tracking of individual transactions, eliminating the need for manual matching of receivables and significantly reducing reconciliation time.
The digitally enabled solution is expected to streamline Square Toiletries’ collection and reconciliation processes while providing greater visibility and transparency across its distribution network.
Sajid Rahman, area head, corporate & institutional banking; Md Rashedul Husain, senior vice president, cash management of Prime Bank PLC, and Md Golam Kibria, executive director; Md Mobarak Hossain, deputy general manager of Square Toiletries Limited, exchanged the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations.
Senior officials from both organizations were also present at the ceremony.
Through this partnership, Prime Bank PLC reaffirmed its commitment to providing innovative and technology-driven cash management solutions that help corporate clients improve operational efficiency, strengthen financial visibility and enhance their overall banking experience.
The initiative reflects Prime Bank’s continued focus on delivering customized digital banking solutions that address the evolving needs of businesses and support more efficient financial management across Bangladesh.

item.title: Brac University felicitates 17 scholars for research excellence
item.description:
Brac University has continued to recognize researchers for a third year in a row, this time presenting “Quality Journal Publication Award 2026” to 17 “Top 2% BRACU Researchers” for publishing in journals ranked within the global top 2% of the Q1 category.
A total of 228 Q1 journal articles have been recognized through the award presentation ceremony at the Merul Badda campus in Dhaka Tuesday, August 25.
In comparison 145 were recognized last year, meaning there has been 57% increase year-on-year.
Among this year’s research, 124 publications are in journals ranked within the top 10% of their respective subject categories, while a further 104 are within the remaining 15% of Q1 journals.
The research of the awardees encompassed a myriad of contemporary issues, such as why microfinance institutions charge higher interest rates than banks and generalized multi-manufacturer multi-retailer production-delivery supply chain model and its minimum cost solution policy.
Of the 21,919 publications made from Bangladesh in 2025, some 4.1% was from Brac University, said Prof Malay Kanti Mridha, director of the Central Research and Innovation Office, at the event.
Research on the readymade garment sector helped determine periods for wage reviews and provide a clear definition of middle management, said Prof Samia Huq, dean of the School of General Education.
Brac University is enhancing industry and national capacity, such as through a video-processing research project funded by Samsung R&D Institute Bangladesh and 8 advanced IC courses under ADP-supported Skills for Industry Competitiveness and Innovation Program, said associate professor Sadia Hamid Kazi, chairperson of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering.
Research outcomes of the Brac James P Grant School of Public Health are now used by the DGHS to monitor non-communicable diseases and helped launch national model pharmacies, said the school’s dean Dr Laura J Reichenbach.
Research and teaching should run simultaneously as students should also be engaged in creating knowledge, said Prof Masuma Habib, member of the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh, as special guest.
Chief guest Abdul Khaleque, secretary to the Secondary and Higher Education Division, Ministry of Education, said the research patterns indicate that Brac University would be the leading educational institution of the future.
“We are used to drawing knowledge from outside, but we have our own BRAC, a huge repository of knowledge,” said Prof Syed Ferhat Anwar, adding that engaging in research synergy was a prerequisite to disseminating this knowledge throughout the world.
The event was also attended by Lady Syeda Sarwat Abed, adviser to Brac Institute of Languages, Professor Emeritus AFM Yusuf Haider of the University of Dhaka, and senior academic and administrative leaders of Brac University.

item.title: BYD CKD Project: Runner Automobiles appoints Green Delta Capital for issuing preference shares
item.description:
Runner Automobiles PLC has appointed Green Delta Capital Limited as the Mandated Lead Arranger to raise up to Tk250 crore through the issuance of Preference Shares to support its Electric Vehicle (EV) & Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEV) project in collaboration with BYD.
A signing ceremony to formalize the appointment was held on August 25, with senior officials from both organizations in attendance.
Runner Automobiles is working with BYD, a leading global manufacturer of new energy vehicles, to develop its presence in Bangladesh's growing EV market.
As part of the collaboration, Runner is progressing towards local assembly of BYD vehicles in Bangladesh.
Under the mandate, Green Delta Capital will advise Runner Automobiles on the structuring and execution of the proposed Preference Share issuance and lead the process of raising the required capital.
The proposed financing is expected to support Runner's investment and expansion plans related to the BYD CKD project, including the development of the necessary manufacturing, extensive testing and operating capabilities.
The transaction also comes at a time when Bangladesh's automotive market is gradually moving towards electric and hybrid vehicles, supported by increasing consumer interest and policy initiatives aimed at encouraging cleaner transportation.
The local assembly of BYD vehicles will enable consumers access to modern brand-new BYD vehicles at affordable prices.
The signing between Runner Automobiles and Green Delta Capital represents the beginning of the financing process for the proposed Preference Share issuance, which will be subject to the necessary regulatory and shareholder approvals.

item.title: Tim Curry, ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show’ star, dies at 80
item.description:
British actor Tim Curry, best known for playing Dr Frank-N-Furter in “The Rocky Horror Picture Show," has died at 80. He died at his home in Los Angeles, California, according to a statement from his manager Marcia Hurwitz on Wednesday.
The cause of death has not been disclosed. Curry had faced health complications since suffering a stroke in 2012.
Curry rose to prominence as Frank-N-Furter in “The Rocky Horror Show," which premiered at London’s Royal Court Theatre in 1973. He reprised the role in the 1975 film adaptation, “The Rocky Horror Picture Show."
His performance as the eccentric scientist became his defining role and helped establish the film as a cult classic.
Curry also earned 3 Tony Award nominations for his Broadway work and received an Emmy nomination. He later built a diverse career across film, television, and voice acting.
Among his notable film credits were "Clue," "Annie," “The Hunt for Red October," “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York," “Muppet Treasure Island," and “Scary Movie 2."
He also played Pennywise in the 1990 television adaptation of Stephen King’s "It," introducing him to a new generation of audiences.
Tributes followed news of his death, including from Susan Sarandon, who co-starred with Curry in “The Rocky Horror Picture Show." Sarandon praised him as a “funny, sexy, original” performer.
Rob Schneider, who worked with Curry in “Home Alone 2," also paid tribute, describing him as a gifted performer of stage and screen.
Curry published his memoir, "Vagabond," in 2025.

item.title: Sadia Ayman, Shafin Ahmed star in short film ‘Aro Kichukhon’
item.description:
Filmmaker Rubayet Mahmud is returning to storytelling with “Aro Kichukhon," a short film starring Sadia Ayman and Shafin Ahmed. The approximately 29-minute film will be released on G Series.
Set in a busy city, the film follows two strangers whose paths cross, leading to a few unexpected moments of connection.
Mahmud said he decided to make the film after years of working primarily in advertising, where he felt there was limited scope to tell stories in his own way.
“I regularly work in advertising, but there is very little opportunity to tell stories in my own way. At one point, I felt that it was time to make a story of my own. That thought led to ‘Aro Kichukhon’,” he said.
The filmmaker said the story focuses on how relationships can create meaningful moments even in a busy urban environment.
Mahmud also emphasized the importance of the screenplay, describing the project as an experiment with a structured screenplay. He said a weak screenplay can prevent even large-budget productions from connecting with audiences.
Sadia Ayman plays the female lead, a role that Mahmud said required subtle emotional expression. He praised the actor for portraying those emotions naturally.
Shafin Ahmed plays the male lead. Having worked in advertising for years as a filmmaker, Ahmed found acting to be a different experience, while Mahmud said his personality and screen presence suited the character.
Mahmud previously directed the drama “Tobuo Bhalobashi” for “Closeup Kache Ashar Golpo” in 2018 and the series “Kabaddi” in 2023. He has also continued working in advertising.
Ripon Chowdhury handled cinematography, while Mazhar Rony edited the film and Chinmoy Roy worked on color grading. Jahid Nirob composed the background score and songs.
“Aro Kichukhon” will be available on G Series.

item.title: Apu Biswas stranded in Nepal amid floods
item.description:
Apu Biswas has been stranded in Nepal amid severe floods and landslides that have disrupted road and air travel across the country.
The actor, who was in Nepal for the shooting of her upcoming film "Shikar," said she is safe in Pokhara and is planning to return to Dhaka.
The disaster has killed at least 165 people, while hundreds remain missing in Nepal and neighboring Tibet. Nepal’s disaster agency reported that 823 people were unaccounted for on Thursday, including at least 579 Nepali and foreign tourists.
Speaking from Pokhara, Biswas said the highway connecting Pokhara and Kathmandu had been severely damaged. She said she had been informed that repairs could take several weeks.
“Our vehicle has been arranged. We will travel to Kathmandu today. There is a lot of rushing for flights. I will return to Dhaka from Kathmandu by flight tomorrow, Friday,” Biswas said.
The actor also asked her fans and well-wishers not to worry about her and requested prayers for her safe return to Bangladesh and her child.
Biswas and the “Shikar” team had been in Nepal for filming when the floods and landslides disrupted transportation. Other members of the film’s cast were also affected by the disaster.
The floods struck parts of Nepal near the China border on Wednesday, with the disaster causing extensive damage to roads, bridges, and settlements. Rescue operations are continuing as authorities search for people reported missing.
The “Shikar” team is expected to resume its travel arrangements once routes become accessible.

item.title: Rupert Grint returns to ‘Harry Potter’ universe in Broadway play
item.description:
“Harry Potter” star Rupert Grint is set to return as Ron Weasley in the Broadway production of “Harry Potter and the Cursed Child," nearly 15 years after the film series concluded.
He will join the New York cast for a four-month run beginning in February 2027.
Grint first played Ron at the age of 11 and appeared in all eight “Harry Potter” films between 2001 and 2011. In the Broadway play, he will portray an adult version of the character, who is married to Hermione Granger and has a daughter attending Hogwarts.
“Dusting off the old robes. New York — see you all in February,” Grint wrote on Instagram.
In a statement, Grint said, "Ron Weasley has been a part of me since I was 11 years old, and I can’t wait to meet him again at this stage of life.”
He added that returning to the role while both he and Ron are fathers feels both familiar and new.
Grint will be the only member of the original trio—Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson, and Grint—to reprise his film role on Broadway.
Tom Felton, who played Draco Malfoy in the films, is also currently appearing in “Harry Potter and the Cursed Child," although the two actors are not scheduled to perform together.
Felton’s run is scheduled to end on January 3, 2027, while Grint is set to begin performances on February 2 and continue through May 30.
“Harry Potter and the Cursed Child” is set 19 years after the events of the original books and follows Harry, Ron, and Hermione as adults. The story focuses on their children and the next generation at Hogwarts.
Grint previously appeared on Broadway in “It’s Only a Play” in 2014. His television credits include “Sick Note," "Snatch," and "Servant."
The Broadway production’s producers, Sonia Friedman and Colin Callender, said Grint’s portrayal of Ron in the films helped define the character for generations of audiences.
The play continues the “Harry Potter” story on stage and has been performed in several cities worldwide.

item.title: ‘How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days’ sequel in development
item.description:
Paramount is developing a sequel to the 2003 romantic comedy “How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days," more than two decades after the original film’s release. Kate Hudson, who starred in the film, is attached to produce the project alongside Stacey Sher.
The sequel remains in the early stages of development, with Paramount currently looking for a screenwriter. The cast and other key creative roles have yet to be finalized.
The studio and filmmakers hope Hudson and Matthew McConaughey will return as Andie Anderson and Benjamin Barry, respectively. However, their involvement in the cast has not been officially confirmed and will depend partly on the script.
The original film, directed by Donald Petrie, follows Andie, a magazine writer who agrees to write an article about how to drive a man away in 10 days.
She chooses Benjamin as her target, unaware that he has made a bet to make a woman fall in love with him within the same period.
Their competing plans eventually lead to a genuine relationship, forming the central premise of the romantic comedy.
Released in 2003, the film was a commercial success, earning about $177.5 million worldwide against a reported $50 million budget.
Hudson and McConaughey have continued to discuss the film’s lasting popularity. McConaughey recently called it one of his favorite romantic comedies and said it remains his most financially rewarding film in terms of residuals.
The sequel comes as Hollywood continues to revisit established films and franchises. However, Paramount has not announced a release date, plot, or production schedule for the project.

Five more children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Thursday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 955 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all five latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.

Meanwhile, 75 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 18,726.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 134,437 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 129,489 have recovered, according to DGHS data.

item.title: Salahuddin: Improvement in law and order now visible, suspects being arrested in 24-48 hours
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Thursday told Parliament that an improvement in the country’s law-and-order situation is now visible, with law enforcement agencies arresting alleged perpetrators and bringing them to justice within a short time after crimes are committed.
“The improvement in the law-and-order situation is visible in Bangladesh. Since the present government took charge, whenever a crime has occurred, the perpetrators have been arrested and brought under the law within 24 to 48 hours or even less time,” he said.
The minister made the remarks, while replying to a supplementary question from National Citizen Party (NCP) lawmaker Md Abul Hasnat (Comilla-4) in the House.
Responding to the lawmaker’s concerns over the law-and-order situation, he said police and other law enforcement agencies have made prompt arrests in several cases, including those that drew significant public attention.
“From the Ramisa case to the four recent murders in Rangpur, the police and other law enforcement agencies have been able to arrest the suspects within the shortest possible time and bring them under the law,” Salahuddin said.
He rejected broad allegations of failure by the Ministry of Home Affairs or law enforcement agencies, saying such claims should be backed by specific incidents and verifiable information.
“If you can point to any specific incident where the ministry or the law enforcement agencies have failed, we can give a detailed response to that particular incident,” the minister said.
He also questioned the basis of crime statistics cited by the lawmaker, saying figures presented in Parliament should be accompanied by their sources and methodology.
Salahuddin recalled that the government previously placed detailed crime statistics before Parliament, including through statements under Rule 300, covering different categories of criminal activities.
Responding to another supplementary question about the number of firearms and the recovery of weapons looted from different places, he said a committee comprising representatives of all relevant forces have been formed to recover the weapons.
The minister said law enforcement agencies are regularly recovering looted firearms and matching their serial numbers to identify them.
“We are continuously recovering weapons, including some of the looted firearms. We match their numbers and inform the media when such weapons are recovered,” he said.
Salahuddin expressed hope that all looted weapons, including those taken from prisons and other locations, will eventually be recovered.
Regarding allegations of political or partisan considerations in police recruitment during the previous government, he said an investigation into the matter is nearing completion.
The minister said investigators have found irregularities involving the recruitment of thousands of police constables and personnel of other ranks in several districts.
In some cases, he said, applicants allegedly changed their addresses to become eligible for recruitment in particular districts, including by purchasing small plots of land and using those addresses as their permanent or village addresses.
Salahuddin said several districts, including Faridpur, Gopalganj, Madaripur, Shariatpur and Kishoreganj, have been identified where such irregularities were allegedly committed.
“We have reached an advanced stage in the investigation. Once it is finalised, we will make the findings public before the nation,” he said.

item.title: Army to build modern arms factory at closed Jalil Textile Mills site in Ctittagong
item.description:
The Bangladesh Army will establish a modern factory on the premises of the closed Jalil Textile Mills at Fouzdarhat in Sitakunda upazila of Chittagong district for producing military equipment and arms, said Chief of Army Staff General Waker-Uz-Zaman on Thursday.
The government formally handed over 54.99 acres of land under the Bangladesh Textiles Mills Corporation to the Bangladesh Army at a symbolic price on Thursday afternoon for the Bangladesh Ordnance Factory (BOF) following an agreement, he said.
The contract was signed between the government and the Bangladesh Ordnance Factories (BOF) of the Bangladesh Army on mill premises as part of the land transfer process.
The factory will help meet the country's demand for arms and could generate substantial foreign exchange by exporting weapons produced there, the Army chief added.
He thanked Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and all concerned for facilitating the land transfer.
“This is not only about meeting the country's needs; the facility will also be developed as an export-oriented industry,” General Waker said, adding that there is demand for Bangladeshi arms in many countries.
If bureaucratic complexities can be removed, Bangladesh could earn significant foreign currency through arms exports, he said.
Explaining the choice of the hilly site at Fouzdarhat, the Army chief said its proximity to Chittagong Port will facilitate the production of modern and sophisticated military equipment and help enhance the country's defence capabilities.
He described the project as part of efforts to strengthen the country's strategic security, saying a long-closed industrial facility will now begin a new chapter in a different form.
Textiles and Jute Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir attended the program as the chief guest.
He said the global defence industry and technology have undergone revolutionary changes, with drones and other military equipment now available at comparatively lower costs in high demand.
The government will provide all necessary support for arms and defence exports, the minister said, adding that the initiative will take Bangladesh to a new level.
Prime Minister’s Defence Adviser Brig Gen (retd) AKM Shamsul Islam and Quartermaster General of the Army Lieutenant General Mohammad Shaheenul Haque were also present.
After the signing ceremony, the minister and the Army chief inspected the abandoned factory premises and later planted trees there.
Jalil Textile Mills began operations in 1961 on around 55 acres of land as a prominent manufacturer of yarn and fabrics. The mill played an important role in the country's textile industry for decades but eventually suffered successive losses and mounting difficulties.
Its production operations were finally shut down in 2004. The premises remained abandoned for years before the necessary procedures and formalities were completed to transfer the land to the Army.
The transfer marks the beginning of a new chapter at a site long associated with the history and heritage of Bangladesh's textile industry.

item.title: Five universities to strengthen systems against campus sexual harassment
item.description:
Five public and private universities will strengthen their institutional mechanisms for preventing and responding to sexual harassment and gender-based violence on campus under a new partnership between the University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh and UN Women.
The initiative will focus on strengthening internal complaint committees, improving reporting and referral systems, and raising awareness among students and staff about mechanisms for addressing sexual and gender-based violence.
The five universities are Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur; Shahjalal University of Science and Technology (SUST), Sylhet; Khulna University; Daffodil International University; and American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB).
UGC and UN Women formalized the partnership by signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) at the UGC Auditorium in Dhaka on Thursday under UN Women’s European Union-funded Ending Sexual and Gender-Based Violence in Public Spaces, Workplaces and in Tertiary Educational Settings in Bangladesh (ESGBV) project.
The initiative comes amid growing concerns over gender-based violence affecting young women, including technology-facilitated violence.
According to the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics’ (BBS) 2024 National Violence Against Women Prevalence Survey, 16% of women aged 20 to 24 experienced technology-facilitated gender-based violence in the previous year.
Through the ESGBV project, UN Women and its civil society partner Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) will work with the five universities to strengthen their internal complaint committees and institutional mechanisms, improve reporting and referral systems, and raise awareness among students and staff.
The partnership will also support implementation of the 2009 High Court directives on preventing sexual harassment, which require educational institutions and workplaces to establish effective mechanisms to prevent and address such incidents.
The project will also introduce social and behavioral change campaigns at the universities aimed at challenging harmful gender norms and promoting safer and more respectful learning and working environments.
Speaking at the signing ceremony, UGC Chairperson Professor Dr Mamun Ahmed stressed the importance of collective action to ensure that higher education institutions provide safe and enabling environments for students and staff.
“True academic excellence can never be achieved in an environment where fear, harassment and discrimination exist. Our universities must remain spaces where students, especially women, can pursue their dreams, explore their potential and express their intellect without the looming shadow of gender-based violence,” he said.
Representing the European Union, Baiba Zarina, deputy head of delegation and head of the Political, Economic, Trade, Press and Information Section, said the agreement could help turn existing standards into practical measures and strengthen institutional responses.
“Today’s signing matters because it could help translate standards into practice, strengthen institutions and give students and staff the confidence that their concerns will be heard and addressed. The lessons generated here can improve higher education across the whole of Bangladesh,” she said.
UN Women Representative Gitanjali Singh highlighted the importance of strong institutional systems, accountability and coordinated action to prevent violence against women and girls.
“Safe campuses are essential for young women and girls to pursue their education and aspirations. It is our collective responsibility to create safer learning and working environments so women can achieve their full potential without the fear of harassment and violence,” she said.
A discussion moderated by Shrabana Datta, manager of the Ending Violence Against Women Unit at UN Women, also highlighted commitments from the vice-chancellors of the participating universities.
The signing ceremony brought together UGC officials, members of the UGC Executive Committee, vice-chancellors and representatives of the five participating universities, along with representatives of the European Union, UN Women and other stakeholders.
The agreement marks another step in the implementation of the ESGBV project, which seeks to strengthen institutional responses, improve access to complaint and referral mechanisms, increase awareness and address social and institutional attitudes that contribute to sexual and gender-based violence.
The broader goal is to create safer and more inclusive campuses where students and staff can learn, work and participate fully in university life without fear of sexual harassment or gender-based violence.

item.title: Rickshaw council warns proposed rules could create vehicle syndicates
item.description:
The Rickshaw, Battery Rickshaw-Van and Easy Bike Sangram Parishad on Thursday urged the government to reconsider proposed licensing rules for battery-run vehicles, warning they could allow business syndicates to control production, charging and operations.
The demand was made at a press conference in front of the National Press Club in Dhaka.
Reading out a written statement, council Convener Khalequzzaman Lipon said the policy proposed by the Ministry of Local Government on August 17 contains both positive and concerning provisions.
Under the proposal, local government bodies, including city corporations, municipalities, upazilas and union parishads, would issue registration and licenses for electric rickshaws instead of the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA).
The council, however, objected to a provision requiring batteries to be charged only with solar power. It warned that violations could result in license cancellation, non-renewal and fines.
It also opposed any requirement to purchase e-rickshaws from designated manufacturers, saying this could create a powerful business syndicate controlling vehicle production, charging, licensing and operations.
The council said nearly 6 million people depend on the battery-run rickshaw sector for their livelihoods, while millions of commuters rely on the vehicles amid a shortage of affordable public transport.
The leaders called for a unified national policy under the BRTA covering registration, route permits, driver training, licenses and fitness certification, instead of a fragmented licensing system.
They also demanded withdrawal of the solar-only charging requirement, an end to extortion and illegal fees, and permission for all qualified local manufacturers to produce battery-run vehicles without preferential treatment for any particular group.
The council announced plans to submit memorandums to the Road Transport and Bridges Ministry and the Local Government Ministry in the first week of September.
It will also hold divisional and district-level rallies and submit memorandums on September 10.

item.title: PM Tarique mourns deaths in Nepal flash floods
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has expressed deep shock and sorrow over the tragic loss of lives caused by devastating flash floods in Nepal and conveyed condolences to the Nepalese government and people.
In a condolence message on Wednesday, he conveyed heartfelt sympathy on behalf of the government and people of Bangladesh to Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah and the people of Nepal.
"Deeply shocked and saddened to learn of the tragic loss of lives, caused by the devastating floods that have struck Nepal. On behalf of my people and Government, I convey our deepest condolences to Prime Minister Balendra Shah and the people of Nepal," the Prime Minister said.
"Our thoughts and prayers are with those who have lost their lives, and with their families and loved ones as they bear this immense loss. We stand ready to extend any support that Nepal may need at this time of distress," added the prime minister.
A massive flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 160 people on Wednesday and left several hundred missing, many of them foreign tourists.
Aid workers said entire settlements had been “wiped out.” Surveillance footage verified by AFP shows dozens of people running for their lives as a stories-tall surge of debris slammed into the Chinese side of a border area, tossing lorries and buses aside.

Iran says US sanctions will achieve nothing
item.description:
Iran's president insisted on Wednesday that the United States would achieve nothing with its new sanctions campaign after Washington laid out plans to collapse the country's economy.
Almost six months into their war, the two sides are locked in a stalemate, with Iran keeping the key Strait of Hormuz shut and Washington persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran.
Under political pressure at home over the impacts of the conflict, US President Donald Trump has pivoted away from military action to economic levers, expanding sanctions and warning of consequences for countries that do not join.
But Iran -- which has already weathered decades of sanctions -- has remained defiant, with officials saying they have a two-year plan to counter the pressure.
"America will not achieve anything with economic pressure at this stage, just as it was unable to achieve anything in the war," Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Wednesday, according to the country's ISNA news agency.
"We will stand firm against economic pressures, as we have done so far and will continue to do."
Iranian army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia, meanwhile, told state television Wednesday that the military had restored its combat capabilities degraded during the war, with the reconstruction of all damaged weapons systems and the import of new equipment from abroad.
On Monday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had claimed the US had "dismantled Iran's military capabilities, destroyed nearly 100 percent of its military factories, and buried its nuclear programme".
Announcing the new economic measures, Bessent said expanded secondary sanctions would target Iran's digital assets and its technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors.
The US and Israel launched the war against Iran in late February, vowing to end an alleged Iranian nuclear weapons programme and threatening to topple the regime in Tehran.
Iran -- which has long denied pursuing a nuclear bomb -- responded with barrages of missiles and drones targeting US allies in the Gulf and closing the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for global supplies of oil and gas.
The waterway's closure has strained the world economy as shipments fail to reach major markets, pushing up the price of oil and placing pressure on Trump ahead of mid-term elections in November.
Trump had frequently claimed a deal was close, but has since backed away from diplomacy.
"I have no time schedule, none. I'm not in a hurry. I have no time schedule at all," Trump told news outlet Al Jazeera on Wednesday when asked how much time he was giving Iran for talks.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday dismissed any prospect of a deal.
"I tell you -- an agreement cannot be reached," he said, calling Iran's leaders "savages".
In recent weeks, the conflict has come to revolve around the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. Iran says it will not reopen the vital waterway until the US meets its demands, and has frequently attacked vessels trying to cross.
Tehran has also indicated it intends to impose fees for use of the strait, which the US and others in the region fiercely oppose.
Trump insists the US navy has "total control" of the strait and has even called it US territory, but traffic there remains at a fraction of pre-war levels.
Oman, which sits on the other side of Hormuz from Iran, has been discussing with Tehran a temporary transit corridor to enable traffic to resume.
On Wednesday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of its military, said the talks with Oman included the two countries agreeing to share any revenues collected from management of the strait, accusing the US of "obstructing work" to finalise the deal.
Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi said on Tuesday that he hoped his country and Iran would "soon announce" the temporary corridor.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi, in an interview with local media, said if the temporary route was agreed, Iran and Oman would have between 30 and 60 days to negotiate a permanent route to replace it.
He added that the Guards were involved in the talks and that the maps under discussion were drawn up by the armed forces.

item.title: Dulu: Immediate legal action if irregularities found regarding fertilizers
item.description: Disaster Management and Relief Minister Asadul Habib Dulu, MP, has categorically said that immediate legal action will be taken against those concerned if any irregularities or unfair means are adopted regarding fertilizers. "There is no shortage of fertilizers and the government is providing a huge subsidy for adequate supply of fertilizers," he said. The minister said this while briefing reporters after attending the Lalmonirhat District Hospital Management Committee meeting on Wednesday, a press release of the Rangpur Regional PID Office said here on Wednesday evening. Minister Asadul Habib Dulu, also the BNP Organizing Secretary for Rangpur division, said that the allocation of fertilizers to the districts has been increased further this year compared to last year. "The government is providing adequate fertilizers and also subsidizing it. As a result, the talk of a fertilizer crisis is being publicized more than the real situation," he said. Noting that initiatives have been taken to increase the number of dealers to make the fertilizer supply system easier, he said that in addition to appointing one more dealer in each union, the number of retailers is also being increased. Informing the government's strict stance against irregularities in fertilizer management, the minister said that the government has adopted a "zero tolerance" policy against any kind of corruption or dishonest means in fertilizers. item.title: Shama Obaed: UNGA presidency to offer Bangladesh greater diplomatic leverage
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Tuesday said Bangladesh hopes to leverage its upcoming UN General Assembly (UNGA) presidency to strengthen international pressure for a political solution to the Rohingya crisis, which she said has grown increasingly complex, with security and other challenges requiring stronger global engagement.
“The matter is absolutely a political problem; it is a very sensitive matter, and we need to solve this problem politically,” she told reporters, stressing that the Bangladesh government is in official and unofficial communication and dialogue with all stakeholders in Myanmar to solve this problem.
Talking to reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Shama Obaed said unfortunately the Rohingya crisis has become more intense and the government is currently trying to solve this problem.
Bangladesh seeks to step up international pressure on Myanmar to find a durable solution to the Rohingya crisis and expressed hope that the country’s strengthened diplomatic position will help advance the issue.
“We are trying to involve the international community more,” Shama Obaed said, pointing to an upcoming high-level UN session on the Rohingya crisis where Bangladesh’s Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is expected to participate.
The state minister said Bangladesh also needs to explore whether the Muslim world can exert greater pressure on Myanmar to create momentum for resolving the crisis.
Shama Obaed said an important high-level session on the Rohingya issue is expected to be held at the United Nations next September, where Bangladesh hopes to secure clearer guidelines for moving towards a solution.
“First of all, I must say that when the Rohingya influx started in 2017, the fascist government that was in power at that time could not play a strong role in solving the Rohingya problem; it failed. If they could have done that properly and involved the international community, then maybe we could have moved towards solving the problem within four to five years, since it started. That did not happen,” she said.
The state minister said a new government has come in place in Myanmar and there is the Arakan Army and other stakeholders in Rakhine State.
She said the internal political situation in Myanmar is also very complicated now and there are many problems along the borders - security problems, various types of crimes being heard - human smuggling, drug trafficking, etc.
The state minister said no one can say the exact number of Rohingyas now because more or less people are still coming every day and an average of 30,000 children are born there every year. “So in that case, we don't know the exact number right now, but it will definitely be over 1.3 million.”
During the recent visit of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to China, the Chinese president said very strongly that he will try to solve this problem and will cooperate with Bangladesh, she said.
On the memorandum of arrangement concerning the Rohingya issue, Shama Obaed expressed scepticism about its likely impact unless the UN and other key stakeholders become more actively involved.
However, she said Bangladesh now has an additional diplomatic advantage through the position of its Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman as president of the UN General Assembly (likely from September 8).
“Now the UN and other stakeholders... and we have an added benefit or a power that now the President of the UNGA is our foreign minister,” Shama said.
She said Bangladesh should use the position more effectively to amplify its voice internationally.
“From that place, we have a power to speak for Bangladesh in the international community. We think that at least in the next year, we will be able to use this capacity a little better,” she said.
Shama Obaed also contrasted the current diplomatic environment with that of the previous government, accusing the then government of failing to exert sufficient pressure on China in pursuing a trilateral arrangement involving China, Bangladesh and Myanmar.
“The then government was not trying, I repeat,” she said, referring to efforts to resolve the Rohingya crisis through the trilateral framework.
She argued that the previous government lacked the political legitimacy and strength to put effective pressure on China.
Shama Obaed said Bangladesh’s current foreign policy is centred on protecting its own national interests while maintaining respectful and balanced relations with all countries.

item.title: President greets Muslims on Eid-e-Miladunnabi
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Tuesday extended heartfelt greetings and Mubarakbad to the people of Bangladesh and Muslims across the world on the occasion of holy Eid-e-Miladunnabi, which will be observed on Wednesday.
In a message, the head of State described the advent of Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) as the greatest and most epoch-making event in human history.
He said the Prophet (PBUH) emerged as a messenger of welfare and salvation for all humanity in this world and the hereafter.
The Holy Quran, a complete code of life and guidance for humankind, was revealed to him, while Islam was established as a religion of peace based on equality, brotherhood and humanity, said Mirza Fakhrul.
The president said Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), through his life and deeds, set an unparalleled example of truth, justice, forgiveness, compassion and human dignity. He upheld the rights of orphans, the poor, the helpless and the deprived, while providing clear guidance on the rights of women, children, neighbours and working people.
He said the lessons of human dignity, rights, equality, justice and mutual responsibility that the Prophet (PBUH) conveyed in his Farewell Hajj (last sermon) remain universal and should always be followed by humanity.
The president observed that the Prophet’s (PBUH) ideals of peace, justice, tolerance, love and humanity are even more relevant in today’s world, which is beset by wars, conflicts, violence, discrimination and intolerance.
He called upon all to draw inspiration from the life and teachings of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), shun hatred, hostility, division and injustice, and pledge to build a just society and state based on peace, harmony, equality and humanity.
President Mirza Fakhrul prayed to Almighty Allah for His mercy, blessings, peace and welfare upon Bangladesh and people across the world. He also prayed for divine guidance to enable all to follow the life and teachings of Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH).

Hog Plum farmers log better business in Rangamati
item.description:
Hog plum is now in season across the hills of Rangamati, with trees laden with the popular sweet-and-sour fruit in homesteads, orchards and along roadsides.
For many Indigenous and Bengali communities, hog plum is more than a seasonal fruit. It has become an important source of income, particularly for women who collect the fruit and sell it in local markets.
The reddish soil and humid climate of Rangamati are considered suitable for hog plum cultivation. Local varieties are mainly grown in the district and require relatively little care. The trees can grow naturally around homes, along roads and on fallow land.
The fruiting season generally peaks during the Bengali months of Bhadra and Ashwin. Hog plum is green when unripe and turns light yellow as it matures.
The fruit is widely consumed across the district. Many people eat raw hog plum with salt and chilli, while ripe fruit is used to make pickles, chutney, juice and preserves.
Hog plum is currently being sold at Reserve Bazar and Banarupa Bazar in Rangamati town, as well as in markets across different upazilas. Retail prices currently range between Tk60 and Tk80 per kilogram.
Indigenous women vendors are bringing hog plum to town in baskets and selling it, helping supplement their household incomes.
Janki Rakhine, a hog plum vendor, said sales remain good during the season.
“Hoc plum sells well during the season. If government support and market access are increased, women in the hills will benefit even more,” she said.
Another vendor, Md Selim, said demand for the fruit is strong in local markets.
“Many customers buy both raw and ripe hog plum every day,” he said.
According to the Rangamati Agriculture Department, hog plum is cultivated on around 24 hectares of land in the district, with annual production estimated at approximately 240 tonnes. The potential market value of the production is around Tk60 lakh.
Rangamati Agriculture Officer Md Moniruzzaman said the agriculture department is assisting farmers by providing improved varieties of seedlings and necessary agricultural advice.
He also stressed the need for fruit-processing facilities to increase the value of locally produced fruits.
“Fruit-processing industries are necessary for value addition to all types of fruit. If processing factories are established in Rangamati, the district’s hog plum could eventually be exported beyond the country,” he said.
However, despite good production, a considerable amount of hog plum is wasted every year due to inadequate marketing and storage facilities.
Agricultural stakeholders say the establishment of cold-storage facilities and modern fruit-processing plants could reduce post-harvest losses and create new economic opportunities for hill communities.
With improved storage, market access and value-added processing, Rangamati’s hog plum has the potential to become an important contributor to the district’s rural economy while opening up opportunities for wider domestic and international markets.

item.title: Upstream water floods homes, croplands in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
A sudden surge of water from India’s Tripura state inundated low-lying areas of at least 15 villages in Akhaura upazila of Brahmanbaria on Monday, submerging croplands, fish farms and vegetable fields and forcing several families to leave their homes.
Residents said water began rushing into the area in the early hours of the day through the Haora River and the Jaji and Kalandi canals following heavy rainfall in the hilly areas of Tripura.
The flooding has affected low-lying areas of Dakshin Union, including Anwarpur, Hirapur, Abdullahpur, Dhaleshwar, Banger Char, Bautla, Birchandrapur, Sahebnagar and Umedpur. Several areas of Akhaura municipality, including Narayanpur, Taragaon and Dhatur Pahila, have also been inundated.
Low-lying areas of Mogra Union’s Colonel Bazar and parts of Moniand Union have also been affected.
Water has entered homes and business establishments around the Akhaura Land Port, disrupting the activities of small traders. Residents of some inundated homes have moved to relatives’ houses for shelter.
Farmers said they were particularly concerned about damage to their crops.
“After spending a lot of money and effort to cultivate paddy, I have now lost the entire crop to the floodwater,” said Abdur Rashid, a farmer from Abdullahpur. “If the water recedes, I do not know how I will cultivate the land again. The government should provide compensation to affected farmers.”
Monu Mia, another farmer from Birchandrapur, said his paddy fields were underwater and warned that continued rises in the water level could cause major losses.
Tajul Islam, a farmer from Rajendrapur, said around four kani of his paddy land had been submerged. He said the crop might still be saved if the water receded quickly, but prolonged flooding would cause significant damage.
Mahbub Mia, a small trader near the Akhaura Land Port, said water entered several shops and business establishments early yesterday.
“If the water continues to rise, the suffering of local residents will increase,” he said.
Abdur Rahim Mia, a member of Ward No. 8 of Dakshin Union, said heavy rainfall in the hilly areas of Tripura had caused the sudden surge of water, which entered Akhaura through the Haora River and the Jaji and Kalandi canals.
Several families have already been affected and taken shelter with relatives, he said.
Akhaura Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Tapasi Rabeya said the administration had assessed the initial damage caused by the influx of water from upstream.
“Thirty-two families have so far been affected, while around 1,400 hectares of cropland are underwater,” she said.
She said the administration was monitoring the situation and had kept local primary schools ready to be used as emergency shelters if the water level rose further.
Dry food, rice, relief materials and medicines have also been kept ready, she said.
However, officials said the situation had started to improve somewhat from the afternoon as the water level began to recede.
Local residents and officials said further heavy rainfall in Tripura could worsen the situation, while a continued decline in the water level could help limit the damage.

item.title: MAF urges Cyber Security Act changes to curb online abuse
item.description:
The Multiparty Advocacy Forum (MAF) has called for amendments to the Cyber Security Act, 2026, to introduce clear legal protection against technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV), saying the law does not adequately address online abuse.
The forum made the demand at a press conference at the Tofazzal Hossain Manik Mia Hall of the National Press Club, where it presented a six-point set of recommendations for a safe, inclusive and accountable digital environment.
Speakers said TFGBV should be recognized as a distinct and serious offence under the law. They said the Cyber Security Act, 2026, lacks clear definitions of TFGBV and “consent” and does not specifically address emerging forms of digital violence, including deepfakes, sextortion, cyberflashing, cyberstalking, doxxing and coordinated online harassment.
Speakers said TFGBV was not merely a cybercrime but a serious threat to human rights, personal safety and the equal participation of women and marginalized communities.
They urged policymakers to adopt the recommendations and make the Cyber Security Act more effective, victim-centered and responsive to emerging forms of digital abuse. They also called for active media cooperation to raise public awareness about TFGBV.
Members of Parliament Nadia Pathan Papon and Sultana Jasmine Jui spoke on the need to include TFGBV in the law and ensure legal protection for victims.
The written statement was presented by Sayra Chandra Chakma, joint general secretary of the central committee of Chhatra Dal, and Golam Mostafa, joint convener of the Bangladesh Youth Federation. The programme was moderated by Enzamul Haque of the NCP and Nasrin Rahman Popi of Chhatra Dal.
MAF Vice-President and Dhaka South BNP Joint Convener Saidur Rahman Mintu, MAF member and central Mohila Dal office secretary Shahinur Nargis, and leaders of various political parties also spoke.
The press conference was held under the B-SPACE project, implemented by Democracy International and funded by the United Kingdom’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO).
